claim: A per-puzzle MDL solver (CompressARC, 76K params, no pretraining) solves 20% of the 400 public ARC-AGI-1 eval puzzles and 34.75% of the 400 training puzzles at pass@2, after 2000 Adam steps (about 20 min per puzzle on an RTX 4070).
schema_part: alt solver for grid puzzles (outside the text schema)
agent_test: Run CompressARC as a side solver on our ARC items; compare solve rate per wall-clock and token-equivalent against the LLM scaffold on the same items.

claim: The 20% and 34.75% numbers come from one team on public splits only. No independent replication or failed replication was found. ARC Prize 2025 reports about 4% on the private ARC-AGI-2 set. Gap search 2026-11-10: still no replication found in 3 further checks (search, repo README, aggregator); the repo README publishes no expected accuracy and no seeds.
agent_test: Re-run the released code on 50 public eval puzzles with 3 seeds; report seed variance.

claim: CompressARC accuracy grows with inference-time steps and with number of guesses. Eval pass@2 is 1.25% at 100 steps, 15% at 500, 19.25% at 1000, 20% at 2000; pass@1000 is 33.75%. The curve is not strictly monotone (21.5% at 1500 steps vs 20.0% at 2000).
agent_test: Plot our own solve rate vs tokens spent on the same items to see whether it keeps rising or saturates.

claim: Pass@1 is 18.5% but pass@1000 is 33.75% on eval: many puzzles are solvable by some sample but not picked. Answer selection (EMA-weighted voting) is a bottleneck.
agent_test: Measure the oracle-vs-picked gap for our agent at equal tokens; test selection by stability under augmentation.

claim: Run-to-run fragility: a needed latent tensor can drop to zero KL and never recover, so the same puzzle can fail on one seed and pass on another. No numeric seed variance is published.
agent_test: Run each item with k seeds and report the per-item flip rate.

claim: The result depends on hand-built inductive biases (symmetry in example order, colour, rotation/flip; 18 tensor shapes; one decoding layer). A plain U-Net trained only on the target puzzle scores 0.75% vs 20%.
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM directly; compare prior-free and prior-rich prompts as an analogy only.

claim: A per-task model trained with reconstruction only and no MDL pressure mostly overfits: Neural Cellular Automata solved 23 of 172 feasible training tasks (13.37%). Architecture differs, so this is not a clean ablation.
agent_test: Compare a no-compression per-task fit with an MDL-regularised fit on a toy set.

claim: CompressARC cannot count, rotate, reflect, rescale, duplicate, chain serial steps, or handle long-range patterns. It is a narrow solver.
agent_test: Check which of our failing ARC items fall in this class; route only the complementary ones to it.

claim: Compute is the main boundary: 130-138 h per 400 puzzles on one consumer GPU, against a 12 h limit for the whole hidden set. It does not fit an interactive agent step.
agent_test: Cost-account any gradient-based side solver in seconds before including it.

claim: Test-time training (per-task fine-tuning on augmented demonstrations) is the dominant 2024-25 ARC method: 8B model 18.3% to 47.1% on the 80-task subset, 53.0% full public validation, 61.9% with program synthesis.
agent_test: Not applicable to a closed API model; test the nearest analogue, demonstrations shown in augmented views, at equal tokens.

claim: TTT ablations: removing geometric augmentation loses 16 tasks (55%); per-task adapters beat shared ones; TTT lifts fine-tuned 5% to 29% on the ablation subset (about 6x).
agent_test: Check whether augmenting the puzzle view (rotate, recolour) before prompting changes accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Selecting among candidates by likelihood under many augmented views improves accuracy: 8B 44.5% (TTT) to 62.5% (16 augmented samples) to 67.6% (product of experts) to 71.6% full system at about 2 cents per task.
agent_test: Score candidates by agreement across re-augmented prompts; compare with majority vote at equal tokens.

claim: Induction (write a program) and transduction (predict output) solve different ARC tasks and combine well (ensemble 56.75% on validation, 61.9% with TTT). Baselines differ between paper versions (induction 35.25% vs 19.25%; transduction 39.25% vs 37.50%).
agent_test: Run program-writing and direct-answer arms on our items; measure overlap of solved sets.

claim: Gradient search in a learned latent program space matches TTT at lower compute on ARC and beats it out of distribution on a synthetic pattern task (TTT 0.3-1.8% vs LPN 88.0%).
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM agent at present.

claim: Small recursive models trained on ARC data beat no-pretraining CompressARC: TRM 7M 44.6% ARC-1 and 7.8% ARC-2; HRM 40.3% and 5.0%. The audited HRM scores 32% on semi-private ARC-1 and 2% on ARC-2; the outer refinement loop and training on eval tasks drive its gain, not the architecture.
agent_test: Test an outer propose-refine loop (1 vs 2 vs 8 passes) at equal tokens.

claim: ARC-AGI-2 is much harder for all test-time-adaptation systems: o3 medium 3.0% vs 53.0% on ARC-1; ARChitects 2.5% vs 56.0%; CompressARC about 4%. Newer evidence: a 200M LongT5 pipeline with LoRA TTT, 18 views and likelihood scoring reaches 27% on ARC-AGI-2 semi-private; Kaggle private top is NVARC 24.03% at $0.20 per task; CompressARC is about 4%.
agent_test: Include ARC-2-style items in any evaluation so we do not overfit to ARC-1.

claim: Language models are strong general compressors (Chinchilla 70B: 43.4% of ImageNet patches vs PNG 58.5%; 16.4% of LibriSpeech vs FLAC 30.3%), and compression of external text correlates -0.93 to -0.95 with benchmark score across 31 LLMs.
agent_test: Not an inference-time test; use only as motivation.

claim: The VAE ELBO is a code length (bits-back). CompressARC drops the weight-cost term, which the authors call reckless. Whether weight regularisation matters is untested.
agent_test: None practical.

claim: Token-level test-time training (TTT layers; nearest-neighbour fine-tuning) lowers perplexity: about 20 neighbours cut bits per byte by 20% on Pile tasks.
agent_test: Compare retrieval of neighbours into context vs none on text tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Agent-framework studies that cite CompressARC do not test compression at inference time. No LLM-agent version of the idea was found as of 2026-11. Gap search found one 2026 LLM-agent paper (Rodionov, ARC-AGI-3) with a prompted simplification step as an MDL proxy; it does not measure description length.
agent_test: Prompt-level proxy: ask the agent for the shortest rule explaining all demos, then compare with free-form.

claim: A prompted simplicity push (replace special cases with shared parameterised rules) inside a coding-agent loop improved mean RHAE over the executable-only variant in 3 of 4 model settings on 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games (e.g. gpt-5.4 xhigh 44.72 to 53.10; gpt-5.4 high 33.54 to 30.60 worse), at 1.6-2.4x the tokens of the textual arm. Single runs, no textual-plus-simplification arm.
schema_part: operator for compression-like simplification of a hypothesis; stopping rule
agent_test: On our items run textual vs textual+simplification prompt at equal total tokens, 3 seeds.

claim: No published measurement uses description length itself (bits or tokens of a hypothesis) as a stopping or selection rule in an LLM agent loop. SOAR selects by count plus 1000 x train accuracy; LLM-PV by held-out validation score; Rodionov by a prompt schedule.
agent_test: Compare tie-breaking by shortest consistent rule against majority vote on our items.

claim: Cost ladder on ARC-AGI-2: Kaggle TTT systems about $0.20 per task (NVARC 24.03% private), Gemini 3 Pro 31% at $0.81, with Poetiq refinement 54% at $31, Opus 4.5 same harness about $60; CompressARC about 4% at about 20 GPU-minutes per puzzle. CompressARC is not cost-competitive on ARC-AGI-2.
agent_test: Record seconds and dollars per solved item for each arm on the same items.

claim: No study tests the open mechanism questions: reconstruction-only control with the same equivariant network, inclusion of the weight-cost term, per-seed flip rate, or overlap of solved puzzles with LLM or TTT systems. The paper's own Appendix K lists the KL floor and weight cost as untested.
agent_test: Run the released code with and without the KL term on 50 eval puzzles; intersect solved lists with our scaffold.

claim: Stability-across-views selection (augment, infer, reverse, vote or score by likelihood over D4 views) is documented only with locally trained models (AIRV 5 to 13 to 39 on private ARC; 200M LongT5 27% on ARC-AGI-2). No closed-API LLM measurement of its gap to the oracle was found; SOAR voting is 5.25 points below its oracle at 30k samples.
agent_test: Ask the API LLM to answer the puzzle on 8 transformed views, invert, vote; compare with single-view and oracle at equal tokens.
